summary: This Dockerfile creates an Ubuntu container with zsh and git installed, then configures a shell function that displays the three most recently modified git branches whenever you change directories or run a git status command. It also sets up a demo git repository with multiple branches at different commit dates to showcase the feature in action.

explanations.3: This tells Ubuntu's package manager to skip interactive prompts during installation, which is necessary in containers since there's no user to answer questions.
explanations.12: The printf command with '%s\n' is being used to write multiple lines of shell script into the zshrc file; each quoted string in the list becomes one line.
explanations.19: This checks whether we're inside a git repository by trying to run a git command that only succeeds in a repo; the redirects send output to nowhere so we just care about success or failure.
explanations.29: This captures the name of the current git branch into a variable so the script can later highlight which branch you're currently on.
explanations.31: The $'...' syntax allows escape sequences like \e[1;36m (which are ANSI color codes) to be interpreted as actual color commands in the output.
explanations.34: This git command lists all local branches sorted by how recently they were modified, and we'll trim it down to just the top 3 with the head command on the next line.
explanations.42: This removes any existing alias named 'gst' so our custom function can take over that name without conflicts.
explanations.63: We're setting the author and committer dates to specific times in the past so the demo repository has commits spread across different dates for testing.
explanations.88: The -i flag makes the shell interactive (so it shows prompts), and -l makes it a login shell (so it loads your profile files like .zshrc).
